Use `Query(max_length=50)` inside `Annotated`, and don't give the parameter a default value. When you need to declare a value as required while using `Query`, you can simply not declare a default value[4]. Since having a default value of any type, including `None`, makes the parameter optional (not required)[4], you should also drop `| None` and `= None`.

```python
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import FastAPI, Query

app = FastAPI()


@app.get("/items/")
async def read_items(q: Annotated[str, Query(max_length=50)]):
    results = {"items": [{"item_id": "Foo"}, {"item_id": "Bar"}]}
    if q:
        results.update({"q": q})
    return results
```

With this, FastAPI will validate the data making sure that the max length is 50 characters, show a clear error for the client when the data is not valid, and document the parameter in the OpenAPI schema path operation (so it will show up in the automatic docs UI)[5].

You can also set a minimum length, for example `Query(min_length=3, max_length=50)`. Note that FastAPI added support for `Annotated` (and started recommending it) in version 0.95.0.[1] If you're on an older version, make sure you upgrade the FastAPI version to at least 0.95.1 before using `Annotated`.[1]
